15.1.title: From wild foods to policy innovation: MMSU's indigenous food plants program as a model for sustainable and inclusive agriculture
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Ma. Concepcion Birginias, Josefa Pugat, Maingeline Vivit, Ruby Rose Tamayo
15.1.summary: Best Paper, sustainable and smart agri-aquaculture and climate resilience category, 2025 SUC-ACAP Biennial Conference and General Assembly (27 to 29 August 2025, Tagbilaran City, Bohol). The paper covers conservation of wild food plants through in situ, ex situ and circa situ approaches and the adoption of the program by the Regional Development Council of Region 1.
15.1.note: Conference paper; Scopus indexing not checked.

facts: 2025 SUC-ACAP Biennial Conference and General Assembly

p: The paper, "From wild foods to policy innovation: MMSU's indigenous food plants program as a model for sustainable and inclusive agriculture", describes the Indigenous Food Plants (IFP) program, which brings together conservation, innovation, policy and education. The program documented IFP species in Ilocos Norte and developed production technologies for crops such as himbabao (alokon), gac (sugodsugod) and latok (kapaskapas).

Conservation follows a triad of approaches: an IFP Botanical Garden (ex situ), a himbabao genebank at the MMSU Forest Reserve, circa situ cultivation of the wild yams kamangeg and dolian, and the integration of IFPs into community foodscapes. MMSU is also advancing omics-based molecular characterization to support conservation and use.
The IFP program is the first R&D initiative adopted by the Regional Development Council of Region 1, providing input for policy advocacy.

p: The NRCMC envisions MMSU to become the research, promotion and conservation hub of flora and fauna in the Ilocos Region, working through inter-disciplinary, multi-sectoral and inter-agency collaboration and partnership. It spearheads R&D on plant genetic resources characterization, conservation of plants, animals and water resources, forest resource conservation and fishery resource management.
Its stated objective is to sustain natural resource health and services, and to establish in situ and ex situ conservation activities for Ilocos flora and fauna.

items.title: Phenological Assessment of Selected Indigenous Timber Species in Ilocos Norte
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson
items.text: Develops a seed calendar for planting-stock production in rehabilitating denuded areas. Suggested collection windows: D. dao August to September, V. parviflora September to October, S. supa May to June, I. bijuga October to November, and A. thurifera April to May.

items.title: Evaluation of Suitable Indigenous Timber Species in Different Site Conditions
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson, Bonne Jovi Orteza
items.text: Identifies promising species for rehabilitating denuded hilly areas in Ilocos Norte. Non-dipterocarps such as V. parviflora, W. pubescens, I. bijuga, S. supa and D. dao are recommended for open and degraded areas; dipterocarps such as H. plagata, A. thurifera and S. guiso are promising but need a compatible species mixture in early growth.

items.title: Fertilizer Management of Different Indigenous Timber Species Under Semi-Arid Hilly Area Condition
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson, Bonne Jovi Orteza
items.text: Finds that 50 g of 14-14-14 plus 300 g of organic fertilizer was enough to improve the growth, biomass, vigor and survival of newly planted indigenous timber species on nutrient-poor hilly land.

items.title: Development of Propagation Management Technology for the Wild Vegetable Alokon (Broussonetia luzonica)
items.people: Maria Concepcion B. Birginias, Menisa A. Antonio, Josefa L. Pugat
items.text: Works out how to propagate alokon by stem cuttings, for domestication and for establishing duplicate mother trees at MMSU. Hormex as rooting hormone and 40 cm cuttings gave the highest survival.

p: On February 14, 2025, to close its 47th Foundation Anniversary, MMSU held the 7th Parambak ditoy MMSU in front of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development, highlighting the impact of its extension and research programmes on community development and agricultural innovation. Thirty-seven exhibitors took part, including learning sites of the Agricultural Training Institute–Ilocos Region, Magsasaka Siyentista (farmer scientists), Balik-Probinsya beneficiaries and local government units, and the Research Directorate gave a speed talk on MMSU technologies such as off-season tomato and shallot production, Bolinao chicken, indigenous vegetables and black garlic.

p: In June 2025, in celebration of World Environment Day, Mariano Marcos State University planted 250 mangrove propagules along the coastal area of Barangay Maglaoi, Currimao, Ilocos Norte, to restore degraded shorelines, enhance climate resilience and promote sustainable coastal resource management. The activity was spearheaded by the MMSU Sustainability and Futures Thinking (SFT) Office with the Local Government Unit of Currimao and led by Dr. Mee Jay Domingo, Vice President for Planning and Strategic Foresight.

MMSU faculty, education support personnel and students joined representatives of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, barangay officials, members of local fisherfolk organizations and community members. SFT Director Dr. Arlene Gonzales explained that mangroves were chosen because they act as natural filters that intercept plastic waste from land before it reaches the sea, while absorbing carbon, protecting shorelines from erosion and providing habitat for marine life.

15.2.1.summary: Graduating classes of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development (CAFSD) of Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU) plant trees before they graduate, and the planting has been repeated every year.
15.2.1.sourceLabel: MMSU News, “BS Forestry seniors leave green footprints with pre-graduation tree planting,” 11 July 2024

detail.lead: Graduating classes of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development (CAFSD) of Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU) plant trees before they graduate, and the planting has been repeated every year.

photos.caption: CAFSD Graduating Class 2026 enrichment planting at the MMSU Forest Reserve, Payao, 1 June 2026. (Photo: MMSU STRATCOM)

p: Graduating classes of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development (CAFSD) of Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU) plant trees before they graduate, and the planting has been repeated every year. On July 9, 2024, the BS Forestry graduating class, led by CAFSD OIC-Dean Charlie Batin, enriched the Salinged Park, the university’s ecological park, with igem-dagat, balitbitan, bitaog, Cassia javanica and banaba. On July 2, 2025, 230 CAFSD graduands planted guijo, yakal and bamboo in the University Forest Reserves in Payao and Mabaleng, City of Batac.

On June 1, 2026, the CAFSD Graduating Class of 2026, led by its Student Council with the chairs and faculty of the Departments of Environmental Science and Forestry, carried out an enrichment planting at the MMSU Forest Reserve in Payao, which the CAFSD Batch 2025 had previously planted with native seedlings. They planted 50 banaba, 30 yakal saplungan and 20 guijo seedlings at the onset of the rainy season, hardened in the MMSU Forest Tree Nursery, species chosen because they improve soil quality, conserve biodiversity and absorb and store carbon dioxide. Dr. Arlene Gonzales, Director of the Sustainability and Futures Thinking Office, represented the University President and commended the college for sustaining the initiative. The activity follows Republic Act 10800, the Graduation Legacy for the Environment Act, which requires students to plant trees before graduation.

detail.lead: Through its Indigenous Food Plants (IFP) Program, MMSU conserves the wild and neglected food plants of Ilocos Norte, 46 of which were documented by the program in seven towns of the province.

photos.caption: Partners receive indigenous food plant planting materials for the Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks, World Food Day 2025.

p: Through its Indigenous Food Plants (IFP) Program, MMSU conserves the wild and neglected food plants of Ilocos Norte, 46 of which were documented by the program in seven towns of the province. The program follows a triad of conservation approaches: an IFP Botanical Garden for ex situ conservation, a himbabao (alukon) genebank at the MMSU Forest Reserve, circa situ cultivation of the wild yams kamangeg and dolian, and the integration of IFPs into community foodscapes.

In October 2025, in celebration of World Food Day, the MMSU Extension and Research Directorates established the second batch of Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks for Indigenous Food Plants with local government units and schools, at Eladio V. Barangan Memorial Elementary School in San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. The foodscape sites serve as seedbanks and learning gardens, and partner communities receive planting materials and technical assistance to cultivate kapaskapas, alokon, pako, dalayap, wild singkamas and roselle. The new partners join existing foodscape sites in Sarrat and Batac.

The IFP Program was adopted by the Regional Development Council of Region 1 as its first research and development initiative, and a study on the program by Dr. Menisa A. Antonio and co-authors won Best Paper in the Sustainable and Smart Agri-Aquaculture and Climate Resilience category of the SUC-ACAP 2025 Biennial Conference, held August 27–29, 2025, in Tagbilaran City, Bohol.

detail.lead: A new season of the MMSU School-on-the-Air (SOA), the university’s radio-based educational program, opened on June 24 and 25, 2025 with 1,000 enrollees from the 22 municipalities and cities of Ilocos Norte.

photos.caption: MMSU School-on-the-Air (Eskuela iti Tangatang) season on regenerative vegetable farming, June–December 2025. (Image: MMSU)

p: A new season of the MMSU School-on-the-Air (SOA), the university’s radio-based educational program, opened on June 24 and 25, 2025 with 1,000 enrollees from the 22 municipalities and cities of Ilocos Norte. The season focused on regenerative vegetable farming for enhanced and sustainable production, with lessons on climate-smart practices and off-season vegetable seeding.

Vegetable growers, rural improvement club members, agricultural extension workers and students followed the lessons, broadcast from June to December 2025 over DWFB Radyo Pilipinas Laoag, DWCI Radyo Adjo Piddig and DWNI Radyo Karruba Burgos. MMSU ran the program with the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte, the Office of the Provincial Agriculturist, local government units, the Ilocos Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development Consortium, and the High-Value Crops Division of Ilocos Norte.

p: On February 14, 2025, to close its 47th Foundation Anniversary, MMSU held the 7th Parambak ditoy MMSU in front of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development, highlighting the impact of its extension and research programmes on community development and agricultural innovation. Thirty-seven exhibitors took part, including learning sites of the Agricultural Training Institute–Ilocos Region, Magsasaka Siyentista (farmer scientists), Balik-Probinsya beneficiaries and local government units, and the Research Directorate gave a speed talk on MMSU technologies such as off-season tomato and shallot production, Bolinao chicken, indigenous vegetables and black garlic.

Participants harvested fresh vegetables at the President’s Farm, 17 new partners of the Extension Directorate received certificates of appreciation, and beneficiaries shared how MMSU’s technologies had supported sustainable agriculture. Attendees included the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte, LGUs, non-government organisations, farmer leaders, entrepreneurs and MMSU-assisted beneficiaries. Incoming President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. urged the units concerned to sustain sustainable farming practices.

The training equipped 46 farmers, local leaders and community members with practical skills in bamboo propagation, nursery establishment and plantation management. Pinili Municipal Agriculturist Philip Galang, representing Mayor Rommel T. p: In 2025, white onion farmer-leaders Mr. Marcos Palacay and Mr. Markflor Valdez of the Ayat ti Pasuquin Farmer and Irrigators Association established a pilot vermicomposting facility in Pasuquin, Ilocos Norte, under the Agri-Tech Facilitator Program of the Farmers Entrepreneurship Program of MMSU and the Jollibee Group Foundation. The facility uses African night crawlers (Eudrilus eugeniae) to convert biodegradable farm waste into vermicast, an organic fertilizer that improves soil structure, stimulates microbial activity and reduces the need for chemical inputs.

The project responds to soil degradation from prolonged reliance on chemical fertilizers, which the farmers linked to poor soil conditions and low seedling survival, and promotes sustainable solutions for white onion farming in the area.

p: On October 28, 2025, the MMSU Extension Directorate, with the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) Batac Branch, held the President’s Farm Field Day: A Technology Showcase in front of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development. Farmers and farmer-leaders, agricultural technicians from Ilocos Norte local government units, BS Agriculture students, and MMSU and PhilRice rice specialists viewed eight rice varieties grown under wet-season conditions.

The varieties included four newly released by PhilRice, two public hybrids, and two suited to saline and rainfed conditions, among them NSIC Rc 686 (Salinas 39) and NSIC Rc 650 (Sahod Ulan 36), giving farmers options for saline-affected and rainfed fields. Speakers included MMSU President Dr. Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr., Extension Director Dr. Marlowe Aquino, and former MMSU President and PhilRice Executive Director Dr. Santiago R. Obien.

15.2.5.title: MMSU Leads Soil Health Research for Rice-Based Cropping Systems
15.2.5.summary: In 2025, MMSU became a key partner in a five-year research program led by Griffith University in Australia and funded by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) and DOST-PCAARRD to develop soil knowledge, information and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems in the Philippines (Project SLaM 2023/146).
15.2.5.sourceLabel: MMSU News, “MMSU tapped as key partner in enhancing PH cropping systems through soil health management,” 31 March 2025

detail.lead: In 2025, MMSU became a key partner in a five-year research program led by Griffith University in Australia and funded by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) and DOST-PCAARRD to develop soil knowledge, information and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems in the Philippines (Project SLaM 2023/146).

photos.caption: Kick-off meeting of the soil health management project with Griffith University and provincial agriculturists, 16 June 2025. (Photo: MMSU STRATCOM)

p: In 2025, MMSU became a key partner in a five-year research program led by Griffith University in Australia and funded by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) and DOST-PCAARRD to develop soil knowledge, information and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems in the Philippines (Project SLaM 2023/146). MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. pledged the university’s commitment at the inception meeting held March 24–26, 2025 in Balanga City, Bataan.

MMSU leads the project on enhancing the productivity of rice-based cropping systems in Ilocos Norte, Tarlac and Bataan through soil health management. Led by Dr. Janet Villamor, it evaluates nutrient management practices and develops yield-calibrated soil health indices for rice-garlic, rice-rice and rice-onion systems. The kick-off meeting on June 16, 2025 at the MMSU Center for Flexible Learning brought together Griffith University, the country project manager and the provincial agriculturists of Ilocos Norte, Bataan and Tarlac, with visits to project sites in Batac, Vintar and Pasuquin.

Manzano Jr. said the paddy art “attracts visitors, promotes research, and showcases innovation,” and Extension Director Dr. Marilou Lucas described it as a statement of commitment to agri-tourism, research and rice appreciation.

On September 9, 2025, the MMSU Dingras Campus unveiled its second rice paddy art, featuring Dingras as the Rice Granary of Ilocos Norte, created by MMSU student planters with PhilRice Ilocos Norte and the Local Government Unit of Dingras. Initiated in 2024, the Dingras paddy art is aligned with Republic Act 10816, the Farm Tourism Development Act, and CAFSD Dean Dr. Charlie B. Batin commended it for boosting agro-tourism and enrolment in agriculture programmes.

detail.lead: On January 15, 2026, officials of the Department of Science and Technology–Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development (DOST-PCAARRD) and the University of the Philippines–Institute for Small-Scale Industries (UP-ISSI) visited the MMSU Crops Research Laboratory to assess a proposed farm tourism project under the Science for the Convergence of Agriculture and Tourism (SciCAT) Expansion Program.

p: On January 15, 2026, officials of the Department of Science and Technology–Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development (DOST-PCAARRD) and the University of the Philippines–Institute for Small-Scale Industries (UP-ISSI) visited the MMSU Crops Research Laboratory to assess a proposed farm tourism project under the Science for the Convergence of Agriculture and Tourism (SciCAT) Expansion Program. The delegation, led by UP-ISSI Director and SciCAT Program Leader Asst. Prof. Melanie Moraga-Leaño, was welcomed by MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. and guided through an on-site technical walkthrough by MMSU’s Vice President for Research, Development and Innovation, the Director for Research, Innovation and Technology, the dean of the College of Business, Economics and Accountancy, and project members from its Department of Tourism and Hospitality Management led by Dr. Eva Jean Viernes. Planners of the Physical Planning and Development Office and the Ilocos Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development Consortium (ILAARRDEC) also took part.

The project, “Project 3. TALON: A Farm Tourism Model for Sustainable Development at MMSU,” is designed to integrate agriculture, tourism and education. It aims to boost the rural economy, provide an alternative income source for local farmers, and offer educational and recreational benefits to visitors by showcasing modern farming practices and technologies. The project has the endorsement of the PCAARRD Directors’ Council and the approval of the PCAARRD Governing Council through an Ad Referendum resolution, and its implementation, led by Dr. Viernes, is subject to the memorandum of agreement between DOST-PCAARRD and MMSU. MMSU is among the select institutions developing science-and-technology-based agri-tourism hubs under SciCAT, which turns farms into tourism sites to promote innovation, entrepreneurship and community development.
